method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Liquid leakage after hard stool in immobility supports retained-stool/overflow assessment before antidiarrhoeal treatment.
Systematic diet/symptom and stool timing/consistency records distinguish patterns from selective reporting.
Privacy/position key is defensible; assembling several staff for encouragement is a weak distractor.
issues: Privacy/position key is defensible; assembling several staff for encouragement is a weak distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Keep the curtain partly open so staff can monitor progress continuously. Explain that observation should preserve necessary safety while reducing the identified privacy barrier.

items.assessment: Easy-release clothing addresses fastening delay; toileting only once per shift is unrealistically sparse.
issues: Easy-release clothing addresses fastening delay; toileting only once per shift is unrealistically sparse.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Schedule a toilet offer immediately before the nurse leaves for each break. Explain that staffing times alone do not address the fastening barrier or individualized urgency pattern.

items.assessment: Observed dryness with cues supports individualized prompted voiding; waiting for spontaneous requests ignores demonstrated cognitive support need.
Prescribed pelvic-floor consistency is appropriate; bearing down and repeated stop-start voiding are recognized technique errors.
Earlier intake is sound; assuming antibiotics without infection cues is unrelated filler.
issues: Earlier intake is sound; assuming antibiotics without infection cues is unrelated filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Use scheduled daytime toilet visits while keeping evening fluid intake unchanged. Explain that daytime scheduling alone does not address the documented nocturnal volume pattern.

items.assessment: Shorter toilet access plus assistance matches retained transfer ability and urgency; catheter convenience is not an indication.
Targeted urinal support is sound; immediate catheter insertion for weak grip is an implausibly invasive distractor.
issues: Targeted urinal support is sound; immediate catheter insertion for weak grip is an implausibly invasive distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with: Offer the urinal at fixed two-hour intervals without assistance holding it. Explain that scheduled access does not resolve the demonstrated grip and positioning difficulty.

items.assessment: Permitted head elevation and positional difficulty support a more natural aligned elimination position.
Observed taut tubing directly identifies traction; securement/slack adjustment precedes assumptions about infection or size.
Avoiding outlet contact and securely closing preserve clean drainage; overfilling/contact with collected urine are meaningful device-care errors.
Gentle external hygiene key is sound; internal urethral scrubbing and pulling the catheter outward are cartoon unsafe.
issues: Gentle external hygiene key is sound; internal urethral scrubbing and pulling the catheter outward are cartoon unsafe.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Use an antiseptic wash at every routine clean even when not prescribed. Replace option2 with: Apply antibiotic ointment around the meatus routinely without an indication. Explain routine gentle care and avoiding unnecessary irritation/products; retain closed-system rationale for option3.

items.assessment: New marks after product change warrant size/skin review; cream alone does not remove mechanical pressure.
Earlier emptying relieves weight traction; extra tape/belt pressure do not remove loading and frequent complete changes can injure skin.
Remove leaking appliance and assess seal is defensible; reducing food to stop all output is unrealistic.
issues: Remove leaking appliance and assess seal is defensible; reducing food to stop all output is unrealistic.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Wait until after the next meal so the appliance can be changed when output is expected to slow. Explain that active burning/leakage requires prompt skin protection rather than scheduling delay.

items.assessment: Refitting for reduced postoperative swelling is sound; pouch deodorant is irrelevant to exposed skin.
issues: Refitting for reduced postoperative swelling is sound; pouch deodorant is irrelevant to exposed skin.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with: Fill the enlarged gap with extra barrier paste without remeasuring. Explain that accessories should not replace correcting an oversized opening as the stoma changes.

items.assessment: Graded participation respects readiness while preserving learning opportunity; immediate full performance or delayed teaching is less suitable.
Checking seal and return demonstration are sound; full pouch safest overnight is an implausible claim.
issues: Checking seal and return demonstration are sound; full pouch safest overnight is an implausible claim.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Adds tape over a small leak and postpones barrier inspection. Explain that a leak needs assessment of the seal and skin rather than concealment.

items.assessment: Individual foods and pouch options support participation; broad diet restriction and certainty that gas ends do not.
All distractors are poor: exact minute, every laxative and louder sounds. Rebuild around realistic outcome interpretation.
issues: All distractors are poor: exact minute, every laxative and louder sounds. Rebuild around realistic outcome interpretation.
proposedChanges: Use alternatives: Bowel movements are now daily but require straining; Abdominal bloating remains despite frequent small stools; Stool frequency has increased but stools are watery. Correct response should retain restored comfort and individual pattern.

items.assessment: Barrier plus gentle cleaning/drying addresses frequent stool irritation; friction and prolonged stool contact worsen skin exposure.
Agreed accessible signal is sound; waiting for a full word and continuously present family are excessively unrealistic.
issues: Agreed accessible signal is sound; waiting for a full word and continuously present family are excessively unrealistic.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Ask a series of spoken questions only when the client becomes restless. Replace option3 with: Place the call bell within reach without agreeing what a toileting request will mean. Explain that a reliable accessible shared signal directly addresses expressive difficulty.

items.assessment: Actual diary/sleep pattern should individualize fixed waking rounds; staffing convenience is insufficient and removing all help ignores residual needs.
All wrong options are irrelevant filler and the key lacks a defined timeframe/frequency despite asking for a measurable goal.
issues: All wrong options are irrelevant filler and the key lacks a defined timeframe/frequency despite asking for a measurable goal.
proposedChanges: Ask which goal best measures the success of a plan to reduce afternoon accidents. Use: No more than one leakage episode during afternoon activities over the next seven days (key); Demonstrate easier clothing fastenings by Friday; Record daily fluid intake for seven days; Describe two continence strategies by the next visit. Explain that the latter are useful learning/process measures but do not directly measure the requested continence outcome.
